proof:
Source: the end of step 3 ("as ζ₀(β₁) = 1 ≠ 0 … r ≥ n"), the last sentence of step 4 (ζ₀(β) = s·β(e'_1, …, e'_n)) and step 5 (normalisation) of the parent proof. Uses the siblings covector_eval_le = Fact (O1) (regcomp_covector_eval_orthonormal_le: |α(τ)| ≤ |α| for every n-covector α and orthonormal τ) and covector_norming = Fact (O2) (regcomp_exists_covector_eval_orthonormal_eq_one: for orthonormal τ there is β with |β| = 1 and β(τ) = 1).
Notation: n = d + 1, p := p_V, r := dim V ≤ n, β∘p := β.compContinuousLinearMap p.
1. (r = n.) Suppose r < n. For every n-covector β and every u, the n vectors p u_0, …, p u_d lie in V, whose dimension is r < n, so they are linearly dependent, and the alternating map β vanishes on them (AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent). Thus β∘p = 0 and ζ₀(β) = ζ₀(β∘p) = ζ₀(0) = 0 for every β, contradicting ζ₀(β₁) = 1. Hence r = n.
2. (Frame.) As dim V = n, V has an orthonormal basis indexed by Fin n (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ V reindexed along finrank ℝ V = n); let v = (v_0, …, v_d) be its image in ℝ^P. Then v is orthonormal in ℝ^P and span{v_0, …, v_d} = V.
3. (Top-degree forms on V.) Restricted to V, every n-covector γ gives an alternating n-form γ|_V on the n-dimensional space V; by uniqueness of top-degree alternating forms (AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det with the basis v of V), γ|_V = γ(v)·det_v, where det_v is the determinant in the basis v. As p u_a ∈ V for every u, γ(p u_0, …, p u_d) = γ(v)·det_v(p u_0, …, p u_d) for all u. (Concretely p x = Σ_b⟨v_b, x⟩v_b and det_v(p u) = det(⟨v_b, u_a⟩)_{a,b}.)
4. (The constant s.) By covector_norming (applied to the orthonormal family v) there is an n-covector β₂ with |β₂| = 1 and β₂(v) = 1. By step 3 applied to β and to β₂, β(p u) = β(v)·det_v(p u) = β(v)·β₂(p u) for all u, i.e. β∘p = β(v)·(β₂∘p). Put s := ζ₀(β₂). Using the hypothesis twice and linearity of ζ₀: ζ₀(β) = ζ₀(β∘p) = β(v)·ζ₀(β₂∘p) = β(v)·ζ₀(β₂) = β(v)·s for every n-covector β. (This avoids constructing the covector β_v(u) = det(⟨v_b, u_a⟩) of the parent proof: β₂ plays its role, since β₂∘p = β_v.)
5. (|s| ≤ 1.) s = ζ₀(β₂), so |s| ≤ |β₂| = 1 by the hypothesis |ζ₀(β)| ≤ |β|.
6. (|s| ≥ 1.) By covector_eval_le, |β₁(v)| ≤ |β₁| ≤ 1. By step 4, 1 = ζ₀(β₁) = s·β₁(v), so 1 = |s|·|β₁(v)| ≤ |s|.
7. (Sign.) Hence |s| = 1, i.e. s = 1 or s = −1. If s = 1, ζ₀(β) = β(v) for every β. If s = −1, let v' := (−v_0, v_1, …, v_d) (Function.update v 0 (−v_0)): v' is orthonormal, span{v'} = span{v} = V, and β(v') = −β(v) by linearity of β in its first argument (MultilinearMap.map_update_smul / map_neg on β.toAlternatingMap), so ζ₀(β) = −β(v) = β(v') for every β.
8. (Conclusion.) dim V = n = d + 1, and the family v (if s = 1) or v' (if s = −1) is orthonormal, spans V, and satisfies ζ₀(β) = β(·) for every n-covector β. ∎
key_steps: If dim V < n then β∘p_V = 0 for every β (linearly dependent arguments), so ζ₀ = 0, contradicting ζ₀(β₁) = 1; hence dim V = n.
For an orthonormal basis v of V and β₂ from (O2), uniqueness of top-degree forms on V gives β∘p_V = β(v)·(β₂∘p_V), so ζ₀(β) = s·β(v) with s = ζ₀(β₂), |s| ≤ |β₂| = 1.
(O1) with ζ₀(β₁) = 1 gives |s| ≥ 1, so s = ±1; if s = −1 flip v_0.
